Converting Seurat, AnnData and SpatialExperiment objects to Giotto

Source: vignettes/articles/converting_to_giotto.Rmd
converting_to_giotto.Rmd

GiottoConnect converts Seurat objects, AnnData (.h5ad) files and Bioconductor SpatialExperiment / SpatialFeatureExperiment objects into Giotto objects with three functions:

  • seuratToGiotto(sobject)
  • anndataToGiotto("file.h5ad")
  • spatialExperimentToGiotto(spe)

All work the same way. They look at the structure of the input, pick the bundled mapping that fits it (for example “Seurat v5 with an FOV image”, “scanpy/squidpy AnnData” or “SpatialExperimentIO layout”) and build the Giotto object from that mapping. Add source = "<directory>" to get a Giotto object backed by a GiottoDisk project instead of an in-memory one.

library(GiottoConnect)

Seurat to Giotto

As an example we load the small Xenium lung crop from GiottoData with Seurat’s own Xenium loader, and run the usual Seurat steps.

library(Seurat)

xenium_dir <- GiottoData::getSpatialDataset("xenium_mini_lung_ffpe")
s <- LoadXenium(xenium_dir, fov = "fov", segmentations = "cell")
s <- NormalizeData(s) |>
    FindVariableFeatures() |>
    ScaleData() |>
    RunPCA(npcs = 20) |>
    FindNeighbors(dims = 1:20) |>
    RunUMAP(dims = 1:20)

Convert it:

g <- seuratToGiotto(s)
g
#> An object of class giotto 
#> >Active spat_unit:  cell 
#> >Active feat_type:  rna 
#> dimensions    : 377, 1531 (features, cells)
#> [SUBCELLULAR INFO]
#> polygons      : cell 
#> features      : rna NegControlProbe UnassignedCodeword NegControlCodeword 
#> [AGGREGATE INFO]
#> expression -----------------------
#>   [cell][rna] raw normalized
#>   [cell][UnassignedCodeword] raw normalized
#>   [cell][NegControlCodeword] raw normalized
#>   [cell][NegControlProbe] raw normalized
#> spatial locations ----------------
#>   [cell] raw
#> dim reduction --------------------
#>   [cell][rna] pca umap
#> nearest neighbor networks --------
#>   [cell][rna] kNN.pca
#> 
#> 
#> Use objHistory() to see steps and params used

The Giotto object holds:

  • the counts and normalized values;
  • the control assays as their own feature types, named as Giotto’s Xenium reader names them (NegControlProbe, NegControlCodeword, UnassignedCodeword);
  • cell and feature metadata;
  • cell centroids and segmentation polygons;
  • the transcripts;
  • PCA (with loadings) and UMAP;
  • the kNN network FindNeighbors() built (as kNN.pca).
GiottoClass::list_feature_info(g)
#>             feat_info
#>                <char>
#> 1:                rna
#> 2:    NegControlProbe
#> 3: UnassignedCodeword
#> 4: NegControlCodeword

On disk

With source, the same conversion writes expression, polygons, transcripts and networks into a GiottoDisk project:

project <- file.path(tempdir(), "xenium_from_seurat")
g_disk <- seuratToGiotto(s, source = project)

AnnData to Giotto

.h5ad files are read directly from disk (with hdf5r); no python is needed. GiottoConnect ships a small scanpy-style file to try:

h5ad <- system.file("extdata", "mini_scanpy.h5ad", package = "GiottoConnect")
g2 <- anndataToGiotto(h5ad)
g2
#> An object of class giotto 
#> >Active spat_unit:  cell 
#> >Active feat_type:  rna 
#> dimensions    : 60, 50 (features, cells)
#> [SUBCELLULAR INFO]
#> [AGGREGATE INFO]
#> expression -----------------------
#>   [cell][rna] raw normalized
#> spatial locations ----------------
#>   [cell] raw
#> spatial networks -----------------
#>   [cell] kNN_network
#> dim reduction --------------------
#>   [cell][rna] pca umap
#> nearest neighbor networks --------
#>   [cell][rna] kNN.pca
#> 
#> 
#> Use objHistory() to see steps and params used

From a typical scanpy/squidpy file the conversion takes:

AnnData Giotto
first integer matrix in X, layers/* or raw/X raw expression
X, when it is not integer counts normalized expression
obs / var (or raw/var for raw/X counts) cell / feature metadata
obsm/spatial (or X_spatial, or obs x/y columns) spatial locations
obsm/X_* dimension reductions (X_pca with its loadings)
obsp/distances + uns/neighbors kNN network (named from the space it was built in)
obsp/spatial_connectivities (squidpy) spatial network
var/feature_types categories one feature type per category

For a large file, convert onto disk; the expression matrices are then streamed from the file instead of being loaded into memory:

g2_disk <- anndataToGiotto(h5ad, source = file.path(tempdir(), "from_h5ad"))

SpatialExperiment to Giotto

spatialExperimentToGiotto() takes the layouts the Bioconductor readers produce. Here the same Xenium crop is read with SpatialExperimentIO and normalized with scuttle and scater:

library(SpatialExperimentIO)
spe <- readXeniumSXE(xenium_dir)
spe <- spe[, Matrix::colSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(spe, "counts")) > 0]
spe <- scuttle::logNormCounts(spe) |>
    scater::runPCA(ncomponents = 20)

g3 <- spatialExperimentToGiotto(spe)
g3
#> An object of class giotto 
#> >Active spat_unit:  cell 
#> >Active feat_type:  rna 
#> dimensions    : 377, 1530 (features, cells)
#> [SUBCELLULAR INFO]
#> [AGGREGATE INFO]
#> expression -----------------------
#>   [cell][rna] raw normalized
#>   [cell][NegControlProbe] raw
#>   [cell][UnassignedCodeword] raw
#>   [cell][NegControlCodeword] raw
#> spatial locations ----------------
#>   [cell] raw
#> dim reduction --------------------
#>   [cell][rna] pca
#> 
#> 
#> Use objHistory() to see steps and params used

The control probes that SpatialExperimentIO keeps as altExps become their own feature types. PCA loadings and variances (scater’s rotation and varExplained) go with the PCA.

The bundled mappings cover:

Input Mapping Converted on top of counts, metadata and reductions
SpatialExperimentIO (readXeniumSXE(), readCosmxSXE(), readMerscopeSXE()) spe-basic spatialCoords; altExps as feature types
VisiumIO (TENxVisium(), TENxVisiumHD()) spe-visium spot/bin positions converted from pixels to microns
SpatialFeatureExperiment (e.g. readCosMX()) sfe cell / nucleus segmentations, transcripts (txSpots), spatial graphs; control probes in the main matrix as feature types

Giotto to AnnData and back

giottoToAnnData() writes a spatial unit and feature type of a Giotto object (the active ones by default) as an .h5ad file in scanpy’s layout, without python: normalized values in X, raw counts in layers/counts, reductions in obsm, and nearest-neighbour and spatial networks in obsp. Networks keep their Giotto names, so reading the file back gives the same object parts.

out <- file.path(tempdir(), "xenium.h5ad")
giottoToAnnData(g, out)

g_back <- anndataToGiotto(out)
GiottoClass::list_nearest_networks(g_back)
#>    spat_unit feat_type nn_type    name
#>       <char>    <char>  <char>  <char>
#> 1:      cell       rna     kNN kNN.pca

In scanpy, use a network by its name: sc.tl.leiden(adata, neighbors_key = "kNN.pca").

Giotto to SpatialExperiment and back

giottoToSpatialExperiment() converts a spatial unit and feature type to a SpatialExperiment: raw counts in counts, normalized values in logcounts, reductions under scater’s names (PCA, UMAP) and networks as colPairs. When the object has polygons, transcripts or spatial networks, it builds a SpatialFeatureExperiment that also holds them (cellSeg, txSpots, spatialGraphs); sfe = "no" keeps a plain SpatialExperiment.

spe <- giottoToSpatialExperiment(g)
spe
#> class: SpatialFeatureExperiment 
#> dim: 377 1531 
#> metadata(1): giottoConnect
#> assays(2): counts logcounts
#> rownames(377): ABCC11 ACE2 ... VWA5A VWF
#> rowData names(8): vf_vst_counts_mean vf_vst_counts_variance ...
#>   var.features var.features.rank
#> colnames(1531): afihnpcm-1 afiiicla-1 ... ogadmnan-1 ogaemdkp-1
#> colData names(11): orig.ident nCount_Xenium ... nFeature_ControlProbe
#>   sample_id
#> reducedDimNames(2): PCA UMAP
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(0):
#> spatialCoords names(2) : x y
#> imgData names(0):
#> 
#> unit:
#> Geometries:
#> colGeometries: centroids (POINT), cellSeg (MULTIPOLYGON) 
#> rowGeometries: txSpots (MULTIPOINT) 
#> 
#> Graphs:
#> sample01:

g_back <- spatialExperimentToGiotto(spe)
GiottoClass::list_nearest_networks(g_back)
#>    spat_unit feat_type nn_type    name
#>       <char>    <char>  <char>  <char>
#> 1:      cell       rna     kNN kNN.pca

Checking a conversion

Every converted object records what was done. mappingProvenance() shows the mapping used, what each parameter was bound to, and what could not be carried over, or was only estimated:

prov <- mappingProvenance(g)
prov$mapping
#> [1] "seurat-assay5"
prov$losses[, c("part_id", "kind", "field", "note")]
#>    part_id                      kind                           field
#> 1     <NA>                   dropped assays/Xenium/layers/scale.data
#> 2     <NA>                   dropped               graphs/Xenium_snn
#> 3     locs                 estimated                           units
#> 4 polygons                 estimated                        geometry
#> 5   points                 estimated                           units
#> 6       nn recovered_from_parameters                            name
#> 7       nn recovered_from_parameters                        distance
#>                                                                                                            note
#> 1                                                           recomputable from normalized values; no Giotto slot
#> 2                                  only the kNN graph is mapped; sNN can be rebuilt with createNearestNetwork()
#> 3                                                                 FOV coordinates carry no unit; assumed micron
#> 4                                       invalid source rings are repaired (make_valid); their vertices can move
#> 5                                                                 FOV coordinates carry no unit; assumed micron
#> 6 Xenium_nn built by FindNeighbors.Xenium.pca on 'pca'; k = 19 neighbours (k.param 20 includes the cell itself)
#> 7            recomputed in pca dims 1:20 (euclidean); weight = 1 / (1 + distance) replaces the binary adjacency

readbackCheck() reads the source again and compares it with the Giotto object, part by part. MATCH means identical, DECLARED a difference the mapping announces (for example a unit that had to be assumed). UNDECLARED would mean a real problem:

rb <- readbackCheck(s, g)
table(rb$status)
#> 
#> DECLARED    MATCH 
#>        1       60
rb[rb$status != "MATCH", ]
#> <giottoReadback> PASS: 0 MATCH, 1 DECLARED, 0 UNDECLARED
#>  status   part_id  aspect   detail                                    
#>  DECLARED polygons geometry 2 of 1531 polygons with a different extent
How a mapping is chosen

findMapping() profiles the object and lists every bundled mapping with its status:

f <- findMapping(profileObject(s), ecosystem = "seurat")
f$candidates
#>                 id version status  coverage specificity
#> 1     seurat-assay   0.1.0   none 0.1111111           1
#> 2    seurat-assay5   0.1.0  match 1.0000000           1
#> 3  seurat-slideseq   0.1.0   none 0.2000000           1
#> 4 seurat-visium-v1   0.1.0   none 0.2500000           1
#> 5    seurat-visium   0.1.0   none 0.1428571           2
#>                                                                     reason
#> 1          param 'assay' could not be bound (Assays value_of: class Assay)
#> 2                                                                  applies
#> 3 param 'image' could not be bound (Images first_of_class: class SlideSeq)
#> 4 param 'image' could not be bound (Images first_of_class: class VisiumV1)
#> 5 param 'image' could not be bound (Images first_of_class: class VisiumV2)

Mappings are chosen by structure (an Assay5 with an FOV image, a Visium image, a scanpy file), not by package version. When a part is stored somewhere else than usual (for example coordinates in meta.data instead of an FOV), the mapping’s declared fallback is used, and mappingProvenance()$alternatives says so. A mapping can also be passed explicitly: seuratToGiotto(s, mapping = "seurat-visium").

Coordinates and units

Giotto uses sdimx = x and sdimy = -y for image-space coordinates (y pointing down), so converted locations, polygons and transcripts are flipped in y.

  • Visium: spot positions are converted from pixels to microns with the 100 µm spot pitch (Visium HD: the bin size).
  • Others: coordinates are taken as stored. Their unit is recorded as estimated, and the conversion warns when the coordinate range does not look like microns, for example scaled to [0, 1].
What is not converted yet
  • Several samples or FOVs in one object: only the first FOV/image is used.
  • Images and Visium scale factors.
  • Seurat SCT assays.

Data that is present but not converted is reported as a warning when the conversion runs, and declared losses are listed in mappingProvenance().
